name: vscode-mlia
description: Run MLIA performance analyses and explore model results in Visual Studio Code.

vscode-mlia.syncModelExplorerSelectionTo.description: Open the corresponding source location when a user selects a node in any MLIA Model Explorer panel.

vscode-mlia.autoOpenModelExplorer.description: Automatically open Model Explorer when an analysis starts and show results when it completes, without changing a newer run selection. New runs become current immediately even when disabled.

vscode-mlia.showCodeLens.description: Show MLIA analysis metrics and source navigation actions as CodeLens items.

vscode-mlia.showHeatmap.description: Show MLIA analysis heatmap colors in source editors.

vscode-mlia.targetProfile.description: Target profile used for new MLIA analyses. Existing analyses are unaffected. Select it from the New Analysis view after refreshing the environment.

vscode-mlia.sourceFileMap.description: Maps source paths from embedded debug information to local source paths. Entries are prefix mappings from an embedded source path to the corresponding path on this machine. Absolute mappings apply to absolute source paths, for example "/root/build-folder/" -> "/home/dev/source-checkout/" maps "/root/build-folder/foo.cpp" to "/home/dev/source-checkout/foo.cpp". Relative mappings apply to relative source paths, for example "src/model" -> "/home/dev/source-checkout" maps "src/model/foo.cpp" to "/home/dev/source-checkout/foo.cpp".

vscode-mlia.configFileContents.default:
# MLIA configuration for analyses started by this VS Code extension.
# Changes apply only to new analyses.
# Supported core settings: https://github.com/Arm/mlia#configuration

[[filtering.collapse]]
kind = "code_stack"
attribute = "file"
globs = [
    "**/site-packages/torch/**",
    "**/site-packages/executorch/**",
]
vscode-mlia.configFileContents.description: Contents of the MLIA TOML configuration file used by analyses started from VS Code. The extension writes this text to its managed runtime and applies it through the MLIA watchdog before each analysis.

vscode-mlia.acceptedEulas.description: Accepted EULAs, keyed by agreement ID and the providing MLIA package version, with acceptance timestamps as values. Accept and Run adds entries here. Delete an entry to require acceptance again, or reset this setting to clear all acceptances. Manually adding valid entries grants acceptance without a prompt. Stored in user settings on this machine and excluded from Settings Sync.

vscode-mlia.extraCommandLineArgs.description: Extra command-line arguments appended unchanged to MLIA analyses started by VS Code. Intended for advanced users. These arguments can cause unexpected behaviour in the VS Code integration. These arguments may also cause EULAs to be accepted without being shown to you, including when they change which backend is used.
